label: Restricted Landauer decoupling: logical erasure ≠ thermodynamic entropy in W33
motivation: Norton & Ladyman (2023) [philsci-archive 22643] proved a restricted Landauer principle: logical erasure is NOT equivalent to thermodynamic entropy erasure for thermal systems. This pass applies that decoupling to W33 machines A and F (the irreversible machines).

norton_restricted_landauer.key_claim: Erasure of logical (epistemic) information via reset operations is not equivalent to erasure of thermodynamic entropy. The Landauer bound kT ln2 per bit applies only when logical and thermodynamic degrees of freedom are coupled.
norton_restricted_landauer.condition_for_coupling: conjugate observable pairs (quantum uncertainty) OR thermal equilibrium contact

thermodynamic_coupling.reason: W33 flag space is a discrete combinatorial object with no quantum uncertainty

w33_machine_A_analysis.landauer_bound_applies: NOT intrinsically — only if physically implemented in thermal contact
w33_machine_A_analysis.note: Machine A's irreversibility is logical, not thermodynamic. The Watts budget of Pass 4337 assumes thermal implementation; the intrinsic W33 cost is 0.

breakthrough: All six W33 machines have ZERO intrinsic thermodynamic cost. The Landauer costs computed in previous passes are implementation artifacts of thermal substrate coupling, not intrinsic W33 properties. W33 computation is thermodynamically free at the combinatorial level.
